 Judgment

Heard Sri. Sharanappa S.Koliwad, learned counsel for the appellant and Sri. Harish S.Maigur,
learned counsel appearing for the claimants.
2. Both the appeals are filed by the insurer of the trailer which is involved in the accident which occurred on 23.03.2016.
There is no dispute over the fact that the motor bike and the tractor along with the trailer met with an accident on that day and rider and the pillion rider of the bike died in the accident.
Two claim petitions are filed by the dependents of the rider and the pillion rider.
The petitions were filed under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.
The Tribunal awarded compensation and fastened liability to the extent of 50% on the owner and insurer of the tractor and 50% on the owner and insurer of the trailer.
The tractor was insured with respondent No.5/insurance company and trailer is insured with appellant.
3. The records would indicate that the bike dashed against the trailer which is involved in the accident.

Under the circumstance, this Court is of the view that the contention of Sri. Sharanappa The Branch Manager vs Smt.Puttavva W/O Somappa on 23 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104755932/
4 S.Koliwad, learned counsel for the appellant that the trailer was not moving and it was the tractor which was moving, therefore, insurer and the insured of the tractor are responsible to pay compensation and no compensation can be awarded against the insurer of the trailer, cannot be accepted.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The records would reveal that the bike dashed against the trailer.
Thus, involvement of trailer is established.
The trailer was attached to the tractor and the tractor was moving along with the trailer.
The insurer of tractor has already satisfied 50% of the liability imposed on the insurer.
4. Under this circumstance, this Court is of the view that the contention that no liability can be fastened on the insurer of the trailer has no merit.

As far as compensation awarded by the Tribunal is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded compensation by taking into consideration the factors mentioned in the schedule under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.
For this reason, this Court is of the view that there is no merit in both the appeals filed by the appellant.
Accordingly, both the appeals are dismissed.
5. Amount in deposit, if any, is ordered to be transferred to the Tribunal.

Sd/-
